newsitem.title: USA: Chinese may have paid lawmakers - report.
newsitem.headline: Chinese may have paid lawmakers - report.

text.p: The FBI is investigating whether China attempted to buy influence among members of Congress through illegal campaign contributions and payments from Chinese-controlled businesses, the Washington Post reported Friday.

The inquiry was begun before the Justice Department created a special task force to examine improper fund-raising practices, including whether there were attempts by Chinese representatives to use their embassy for planning contributions to the Democratic National Committee before the 1996 election, the newspaper said.
A spokesman for the Chinese embassy has flatly denied the allegations of improper fund-raising activities.

The Post reported a witness interviewed by FBI agents assigned to the task force said he was told the focus of the Justice Department inquiry was to determine whether members of both parties in Congress had been improperly influenced by Chinese representatives who might have made illegal payments to them.
Government officials quoted by the newspaper said the FBI had not yet identified specific members of Congress who might have received illegal or improper payments.

Secretary of State Madeleine Albright raised "concern" during her recent visit to Beijing about news reports that the Chinese might be trying improperly to influence American policy with campaign money, the Post reported.
Albright told Chinese officials she was sensitive to their denials and her remarks were "low key and informal," according to the newspaper.

The Justice Department task force was trying to learn whether Chinese representatives had directed payments to U.S. officials through corporations controlled by the government in Beijing, in violation of federal laws, the Post said.
